chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seventy times a day. So I said, 'Did he say: I seek forgiveness of Allah and I turn to Him?' He said, 'No, but he used to say: I turn to Allah.' I said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) repented and did not repeat, while we repent and repeat.' So he said, 'Allah is the One sought for help.'

key_terms.اللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ: Allah is the One sought for help
key_terms.لَا يَعُودُ: did not repeat / did not return (to sin)

ai.seo_question: What was the specific phrase used by Prophet Muhammad for his daily repentance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) engaged in constant repentance (tawab) not due to sin, but as an expression of perpetual humility and closeness to Allah, distinguishing his state of perfection from human repentance necessitated by recurring faults. This narration underscores the Shia theological view that the Prophet's 'repentance' is a continuous act of worship and gratitude rather than a remedial response to error. Such frequent invocation highlights the spiritual discipline expected of the faithful, mirroring the Prophet's example of unwavering devotion.
